title: Peruvian Lomo Saltado
subtitle: stir-fried beef with chips and rice
excerpt: Strips of beef, onion, and tomato stir-fried together with soy sauce and vinegar, then served over rice and chips. This is one of Peru's great dishes -- a direct result of Chinese immigration to South America.
sourceNotes: Lomo saltado is a signature dish of Peruvian-Chinese cooking, known as chifa. Chinese immigrants arrived in Peru in the 19th century and merged their cooking traditions with local ingredients.

content.text: The heat must be very high for this dish. Everything cooks fast. Have all ingredients ready before you turn the heat on. The stir-fry should take only a few minutes from start to finish.

items.prepNote: use rump or sirloin steak, cut into strips
cut into chips and fried or oven-baked separately
use a handful of fresh coriander leaves

content.text: Cook the rice according to packet instructions. Keep warm.
Fry or oven-bake the chips until golden and crispy. Keep warm.
Heat a cast-iron skillet over the highest heat possible until very hot.
Season the beef with salt. Fry in the hot pan in a single layer for 1 to 2 minutes until seared. Remove and set aside.
Add the onion and peppers to the pan. Stir-fry for 2 minutes over high heat.
Add the garlic and tomato wedges. Cook for 1 minute.
Return the beef to the pan. Add the soy sauce and worcestershire sauce. Toss everything together for 1 minute.
Add the chips to the pan and toss briefly. Scatter with fresh coriander.
Serve immediately on top of rice.

items.symptom: Beef is tough instead of tender
items.cause: Wrong cut or pan not hot enough
items.fix: Use rump or sirloin for stir-frying. Chuck is better for slow cooking. High heat and a fast cook are essential.

items.cause: Pan not hot enough or too many vegetables at once
items.fix: Cook in batches if your pan is not very large. High heat cooks them fast and keeps them with texture.

items.symptom: Chips go soft in the pan
items.cause: Added too early or pan steaming
items.fix: Add the chips right at the end, just to warm and coat them. They should keep their crunch.

content.text: Lomo saltado is one of Peru's most popular dishes. It comes from the chifa tradition -- Peruvian-Chinese cooking. Chinese immigrants arrived in Peru in the 19th century and brought stir-fry technique with them. The dish mixes that technique with Peruvian ingredients like chilli and potato.
